stop alternative with additional formatting (Experimental)

Source: R/conditions.R
stopit.Rd

stopit() can be used in place of stop with additional formatting enabled by super::glue() allowing embraced expressions to be looked up in the provided environment (akin to calling get()). Single braces can be escaped by doubling them up. Messages of length > 1 will have the second elements onwards indented for clarity. Unerlying conditions will have class <(.subclass)/ympesError/error/condition>.

Usage

stopit(
  msg = "",
  ...,
  .subclass = NULL,
  .call = sys.call(-1L),
  .env = parent.frame(),
  .domain = NULL
)

Arguments

msg

[character string]

The message to be used in the error condition.

...

Additional fields to be used in the underlying error condition.

.subclass

[character]

The (optional) subclass of the returned error condition.

Conditions will have class <(.subclass)/ympesError/error/condition>.

.call

[call]

Call to use in error message.

.env

[environment]

Where to look up the embraced input.

Can be an environment or a list-like object that will be converted in the underlying function via list2env().

.domain

The ‘domain’ for the translation, a character string, or NULL.

See gettext().

Examples


f <- function(x) {
    if (x < 1)
        stopit(c("`x` must be > 1", "you entered x = {x}"))
    x^2
}
tryCatch(f(0), error = function(cnd) cat(conditionMessage(cnd)))
#> 
#> `x` must be > 1
#>       - you entered x = 0
